name: Steve Fuller
note: Elected 17 April 1979, defeating Tom Jecker, a Louisville senior, 973-574. He was elected ASG president a year later, in April 1980.

name: Dean Bates
note: A Fairport, N.Y., junior, elected activities vice president 17 April 1979 over Ben Bratcher, a Louisville senior, 785-761 - the closest of the executive races, and the first election to the office after the Regents moved lectures and concerts to the University Center Board on 31 March 1979.

name: Betty Thompson
note: A Bowling Green junior, elected secretary over Lynn Driver, a Goodlettsville, Tenn., sophomore, 1,052-517.

name: Terri Craig
note: A St. Joseph, Ill., junior, elected treasurer over Darell Pierce, a Louisville junior, 937-623.

name: Mark Wilson
note: A Shelbyville student, elected 22 April 1980 over Michael Allen Baker, a Cincinnati senior, 821-342; the Herald's results list printed the office as "administrative president", while the 1981 Talisman calls him administrative vice president. He led the opposition to M.A. Baker's resolution to abolish dormitory room inspections, saying "Public safety comes at the expense of the individual's absolute rights"; ASG defeated the resolution 16-13 and a second attempt 24-9.
quote: Public safety comes at the expense of the individual's absolute rights.
photo_lead: 1981 Talisman, Associated Student Government section, photograph captioned "ADMINISTRATIVE VICE PRESIDENT Mark Wilson, a Shelbyville junior" (pp. 282-283)

name: Greg Zoeller
note: A Louisville senior, elected activities vice president 22 April 1980 over Edmond Schwab, a Bowling Green senior, 937-217. His was the last election held under that title; the office was called public affairs vice president by the following April.
photo_lead: 1981 Talisman, Associated Student Government group photograph, third row, names in caption (pp. 282-283)

name: Marsha Sanner
note: An Orchard Lake, Mich., junior, elected secretary unopposed in the April 1980 general election.
photo_lead: 1981 Talisman, Associated Student Government group photograph, front row, names in caption (pp. 282-283)

name: Mark Chesnut
note: A Bowling Green junior, elected treasurer unopposed in the April 1980 general election.

name: Paul J. Deom
note: Wrote to the Herald in February 1982 that he had been appointed to the Judicial Council in the autumn of 1980 by then-president Steve Fuller on the understanding that the term ran two years, and that the executive council and president had since replaced him. He listed his grievances, among them a Washington trip taken by three executive officers without consulting congress.

name: Margaret Ragan
note: Elected to the vacant administrative vice presidency by congress in January 1982 after David Payne moved up to president, defeating Doug Ball; congress unanimously approved the result. As administrative vice president she announced the swearing-in of the new seven-member Judicial Council, describing it as "a good cross-section of the university", and as complaints and suggestions committee chairman she asked the city for a four-way stop at Normal Drive and University Boulevard.
quote: a good cross-section of the university

name: Laura Simms
note: Elected 7 April 1981 over Kevin Francke, 839-351, the first person elected under the new title. In February 1982 she defended the appointment of the president's roommate to the Judicial Council, saying she believed he could remain objective.

name: Alesia Canafax
note: Elected secretary 7 April 1981 over Anne McKee, 661-500. As rules and elections committee chairwoman she refused to certify the 13 April 1982 general election after the voting register and the ballot count disagreed, and requested the repeat election that adviser Ron Beck approved.

name: Greg Jennings
note: Elected treasurer 7 April 1981 over James Lynch, 597-566.

name: Gale Williams
note: An Elizabethtown senior, sworn in as chairman of the new seven-member Judicial Council at the ASG meeting of 26 January 1982 after congress approved the appointments by the required two-thirds.

name: Bob Dillard
note: A Bowling Green student sworn in to the Judicial Council in January 1982. Because he was President David Payne's roommate the appointment was publicly questioned as a conflict of interest; Dillard said Payne would not influence his decisions, Payne said he had the power to appoint whom he chose, and adviser Ron Beck said he thought Dillard was one of the best people for the job.

name: Regenia Giles
note: A Hopkinsville junior, sworn in to the Judicial Council at the ASG meeting of 26 January 1982.

name: Rick Murphy
note: A Bowling Green senior, sworn in to the Judicial Council at the ASG meeting of 26 January 1982.

name: Dave Hoffmann
note: A Fort Mitchell sophomore, sworn in to the Judicial Council at the ASG meeting of 26 January 1982.

name: Jill Capps
note: A Bowling Green sophomore, sworn in to the Judicial Council at the ASG meeting of 26 January 1982.

name: Archie Beck
note: A Russellville senior named to the Judicial Council in January 1982; he was absent from the swearing-in and Ragan said he would be sworn in later.

name: Jack Smith
note: A Prospect junior, elected administrative vice president in the repeat general election of 20 April 1982, beating Doug Ball, a Louisville junior, 533-102. He was elected ASG president a year later.

name: Kerrie Stewart
note: A LaCenter sophomore, elected public affairs vice president in the repeat general election of 20 April 1982, beating Jack Murphree, a junior from Nashville, Tenn., 440-145. The Herald reported that she died of a heart condition during the following summer, and that ASG members selling discount-card advertising could donate their commission to the Kerrie Stewart Scholarship.

name: Tony Whalen
note: A Louisville junior, elected administrative vice president 12 April 1983, defeating David Dilley, a Greenville junior, 475-330. Planning the new term, he said committee chairmen should take the roll at each session and that a member who missed three committee meetings should have to explain the absences to the executive officers.

name: William "Happy" Chandler
note: A Valley Station senior, elected public affairs vice president 12 April 1983 over Kim Binkley, a sophomore from Springfield, Tenn., 477-379. He announced the plan under which ASG members earned a 20 percent commission for signing businesses to the student discount card, said the advertisements would sell for $100 each, and proposed that executive officers meet freshmen during orientation.

name: Teresa Anthony
note: A Greenville junior, elected secretary 12 April 1983 over Claire Groemling, a Louisville junior, 464-324.

name: Kelly S. Smith
note: A sophomore from Gallatin, Tenn., elected treasurer unopposed on 12 April 1983 after Patrick McLaughlin, a Louisville sophomore, dropped out of the race.

name: Mark Rawlings
note: Appointed mid-year: the President reported interviewing four candidates for the vacant Vice President of Finance post, and Rawlings was approved by Congress and sworn in on 16 January 2001. Amy Caswell had been elected to the office in April 2000.

name: Joe Morel
note: Sworn in as a Justice on 30 January 2001, the same night three at-large members joined Congress.

name: Holly Skidmore
note: Appointed and sworn in as Public Relations chairperson on 16 January 2001; she had been collecting proposals for the SGA display board.

name: Jamie Sears
note: Chaired Congress, organised the fall retreat and circulated its evaluation questionnaires, and appointed the Sergeant-at-Arms. Elected SGA president for 2002-03.
src_label: SGA website, "Meet Your Executive Council", 7 Jan 2002 (Internet Archive)
photo_lead: Archived SGA site, officer profile page wku.edu/sga/jamie.htm (11 Mar 2002 capture), portrait at images/Jamie.jpg with her name and office in the heading

name: Aaron Spencer
note: Presented the 2001-2002 SGA budget to Congress for review on 11 September 2001 and for a vote the following week. A senior marketing major from Madisonville who had been vice chair of the Legislative Research Committee.
photo_lead: Archived SGA site, officer profile page wku.edu/sga/aaron.htm (11 Mar 2002 capture), portrait at images/Aaron.jpg captioned with his name and office

name: Mark Rawlings
note: Ran homecoming packets and the September 2001 Red Cross blood drive, and presented a hard-work award to Jamie Sears for organising the fall retreat. He had held the Vice President of Finance office the previous January.
photo_lead: Archived SGA site, officer profile page wku.edu/sga/mark.htm (11 Mar 2002 capture), portrait at images/Mark.jpg captioned with his name and office

name: Jamil Sewell
note: Kept and signed the weekly minutes, conducted the swearing-in of new Congress members, and sat on the Constitutional Review Committee appointed in October 2001. He had co-authored Bill 99-10-F creating the Information Technology Director.

name: Adam Leach
note: Appointed by the Executive Vice President and approved by Congress on 4 September 2001.

name: Dana Lockhart
note: Appointed Parliamentarian on 11 September 2001; the post had been reported open the week before.

name: Dwight Campbell
note: Appointed Parliamentarian by the Executive Vice President on 29 January 2002, succeeding Dana Lockhart.

name: Andrea Lovell
note: Appointed at the first Congress meeting of the year, 4 September 2001, and reported weekly on the committee heads' meetings.

name: Heidi Grogg
note: Sworn in as a member of the Judicial Council on 11 September 2001 and listed as Chief Justice on SGA's own website through the year.
src_label: SGA website, Judicial Council, 15 Apr 2002 (Internet Archive)

name: Brandon Copeland
note: Sworn in to the Judicial Council on 11 September 2001 and named to the Constitutional Review Committee that October. Elected Vice President of Administration for 2002-03.
src_label: SGA website, Judicial Council, 15 Apr 2002 (Internet Archive)

name: Robert Unseld Jr.
src_label: SGA website, Judicial Council, 15 Apr 2002 (Internet Archive)

name: Amanda Demarest
note: Sworn in to the Judicial Council on 11 September 2001 alongside Heidi Grogg and Brandon Copeland.
src_label: SGA website, Judicial Council, 15 Apr 2002 (Internet Archive)

name: Mike Richardson
note: Sworn in as an associate Judicial Council member on 16 October 2001; in the spring he delivered the council's reports to Congress as its Clerk, including its ruling that candidates and their staff could not remove campaign posters.

name: Shara Hammers
note: Appointed committee head on 4 September 2001, and chaired the Constitutional Review Committee the President appointed on 16 October 2001.

name: John Bradley
note: Appointed committee head on 4 September 2001; his committee reported it had ideas enough for legislation within a fortnight. Elected Executive Vice President for 2002-03.

name: Amy Caswell
note: Appointed committee head on 4 September 2001. She had been elected Vice President of Finance for 2000-01.

name: Anna Coats
note: Appointed committee head on 4 September 2001; her committee priced Provide-a-Ride magnets and ran a recruitment table in September. Elected Vice President of Public Relations for 2002-03.

name: Sam Stinson
note: Appointed by the President and sworn in on 27 August 2002; he built and maintained the SGA website, posted candidate profiles and pictures, and reported being swamped with new material. He had run for SGA president that April.

name: Eddie Schwab
note: Appointed by the President and sworn in on 27 August 2002 after Congress suspended the bylaws to approve the Historian and IT Director together.

name: Dwight Campbell
note: Named Parliamentarian in the Vice President's appointments at the first Congress meeting of the year, 27 August 2002.

name: Brooke Smith
note: Appointed by Vice President John Bradley on 17 September 2002 and approved unanimously the following week; she had brought the petition for a writ of certiorari over the gazebo funds and withdrew it once the ad hoc Financial Review Committee was created.

name: Dana Lockhart
note: Announced as Parliamentarian among the appointments of 25 February 2003. She had reported for the Judicial Council and for the University Senate through the autumn.

name: Michelle Woods
note: Appointed on 27 August 2002 and ran the weekly committee heads' meeting.

name: Holly Skidmore
note: Named Chief Justice in the President's appointments of 27 August 2002 and sworn in on 3 September when she and Mark Rawlings were both present.

name: Dana Lockhart
note: Reported the council's work to Congress on 17 September 2002 - five requests for judicial interpretation considered at its first meeting - and told Congress all requests for interpretation had to be in writing.

name: Ellen Fox
note: Sworn in to the Judicial Council on 27 August 2002.

name: Adam Leach
note: Named to the Judicial Council in the President's appointments of 27 August 2002. He had been Sergeant-at-Arms the previous year.

name: Mark Rawlings
note: Named to the Judicial Council on 27 August 2002 and sworn in on 3 September. He had been Vice President of Finance in 2000-01 and Vice President of Public Relations in 2001-02.

name: Diana Carag
note: Announced as a Judicial Council appointment on 25 February 2003, when Congress suspended the bylaws to vote on the appointments.

name: Scott Wolfe
note: Appointed committee head on 27 August 2002; his committee approved an LRC checklist and carried Bill 02-02-F, the SGA Archivist, to Congress.

name: Jessica Martin
note: Appointed committee head on 27 August 2002; she was also an SGA appointee to the University Senate. Elected Vice President of Administration for 2003-04.

name: Charlie Walker
note: Appointed committee head on 27 August 2002. SGA's own website spells the name Charley on its Student Affairs Chair page; the minutes and the 2002 primary results both give Charlie, and the spelling is unresolved.
photo_lead: Archived SGA site, Student Affairs Chair page wku.edu/sga/sacchair.html (25 Feb 2003 capture), portrait at c2002/images/walker.jpg beside his name and office

name: Patti Johnson
note: Appointed committee head on 27 August 2002. Elected Executive Vice President for 2003-04.

name: Kristin Hartley
note: Appointed committee head on 27 August 2002; her committee replaced the traditional dinner with a dessert reception and began recognising a senior each week.

name: Nick Todd
note: Listed as Campus Improvements chair on SGA's Congress member page, and appointed chair of the ad hoc Financial Review Committee on 17 September 2002 to examine the gazebo spending. Elected Vice President of Finance for 2003-04.
src_label: SGA website, Congress member profile, 17 Nov 2002 (Internet Archive)

name: Katie Dawson
note: Appointed by the President with Tim Howard as the new Student Affairs co-chairs on 29 January 2003 and approved unanimously.

name: Tim Howard
note: Appointed with Katie Dawson as Student Affairs co-chair on 29 January 2003.

name: Kyle Gott
note: Nominated by the President on 11 March 2003 and approved unanimously after Congress suspended the bylaws to take the vote.

name: Patti Johnson
note: Won the office on 8 April 2003 with 1,185 votes to Dana Lockhart's 685, chaired Congress all year, and appointed the Sergeant-at-Arms and Parliamentarian. SGA's own executive page also listed her simply as Vice President.
src_label: SGA website, 2003 election results, 25 Apr 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Nick Todd
note: Elected unopposed with 1,661 votes; he put the 2003-2004 budget to Congress on 2 September 2003, where it passed unanimously after he argued against dropping Buy-A-Book, saying SGA should help who it can.
src_label: SGA website, 2003 election results, 25 Apr 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Jessica Martin
note: Won the office on 8 April 2003 with 1,056 votes to Shawn Peavie's 686, kept and signed the weekly minutes, and pressed Congress members to attend so the new constitution could reach a two-thirds vote.
src_label: SGA website, 2003 election results, 25 Apr 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Abby Lovan
note: Elected unopposed with 1,694 votes; she ran the member-profile and t-shirt work, oversaw the website relaunch with the IT designate, and was nominated for Speaker of the Senate in April 2004 before withdrawing.
src_label: SGA website, 2003 election results, 25 Apr 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Matthew Pava
note: Reported to Congress each week on the SGA website through 2003-04. The minutes head his report "Information Technology Designate"; the same officer is called Information Technology Director elsewhere in the year's minutes.

name: Cameron Yancey
note: Approved and sworn in on 16 September 2003, three weeks after the Executive Vice President told Congress the post was hers to fill.

name: Mason Stevenson
note: Approved and sworn in with Cameron Yancey on 16 September 2003.

name: Scott Wolfe
note: Held the coordinator's seat from the start of the year and was still reporting in January 2004. He had chaired the Legislative Research Committee in 2002-03.
src_label: SGA website, Legislative Branch 2003-2004, 23 Sep 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Brittany Fausey
note: Approved as the new Coordinator of Committees on 2 March 2004, succeeding Scott Wolfe; she had co-chaired the Public Relations Committee.

name: Troy Ransdell
note: Approved and sworn in as Chief Justice on 2 September 2003, then swore in three of the four justices and the committee heads the same night; his council elected him its delegate to speak to Congress and he also sat on the University Senate.

name: Gretchen Light
note: Elected secretary of the Judicial Council at its first meeting on 8 September 2003. A sophomore from Newburgh, Indiana, who had been secretary of the Legislative Research Committee.
src_label: SGA Judicial Council minutes, 8 Sep 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Josh Collins
note: Sworn in on 2 September 2003 and present at the council's first meetings; he was also named to the University Senate's Academic Quality ad hoc committee in November 2003.
src_label: SGA Judicial Council minutes, 8 Sep 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Scott Broadbent
note: Sworn in on 2 September 2003. The council's minutes of 8 September record the same seat under the name Scott Jaggers and those of 22 September under Scott Broadbent, which is also the name SGA's website used; the discrepancy is unresolved.
src_label: SGA website, Judicial Branch 2003-2004, 23 Sep 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Kristin Hartley
note: Listed as the fifth justice on SGA's website on 23 September 2003; the council's minutes of 22 September still recorded the fifth seat as unfilled.
src_label: SGA website, Judicial Branch 2003-2004, 23 Sep 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Robert Watkins
note: Wrote Bill 03-10-F, the new constitution and bylaws, and defended it before Congress on 2 December 2003, saying the old constitution had too many problems; he also asked the Judicial Council for the ruling that replaced "Academic Council" with "University Senate" in the governing documents.

name: Robert Watkins
note: Elected the first Speaker of the Senate by secret ballot on 13 April 2004, beating Brittany Fausey by one vote after Abby Lovan withdrew her nomination.

name: Natalie Croney
note: Sworn in as a committee head on 2 September 2003 and still chairing in January 2004.
src_label: SGA website, Legislative Branch 2003-2004, 23 Sep 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Shawn Peavie
note: Defended Resolution 03-13-F on re-gravelling the SkyPAC parking lot and Bill 03-11-F, the SGA Adopt-A-Tree Program, on 2 December 2003; both passed. SGA's 2003 election results page spells the name Sean.

name: Katie Dawson
note: Defended Resolution 03-14-F on private information security in December 2003 and Resolution 04-03-S opposing a broadband expansion fee in April 2004, telling Congress a survey of 400 students showed they did not want the fee.

name: Tim Howard
src_label: SGA website, Legislative Branch 2003-2004, 23 Sep 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Brittany Fausey
note: Sworn in as a committee head on 2 September 2003; she lost the Speaker of the Senate ballot to Robert Watkins by one vote in April 2004 and became Coordinator of Committees in March.
src_label: SGA website, Legislative Branch 2003-2004, 23 Sep 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Evelina Petkova
note: A junior from Sofia, Bulgaria, who had been secretary of the Public Relations Committee before co-chairing it.
src_label: SGA website, Legislative Branch 2003-2004, 23 Sep 2003 (Internet Archive)

name: Stacey Adkisson
src_label: SGA website, Legislative Branch 2003-2004, 23 Sep 2003 (Internet Archive)
